title: Coherence of a module is local on an open covering
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ a covering by open subschemes; for an open $W\subseteq X$ write $\mathcal F|_W$ for the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subscheme $W$ ($(\mathcal F|_W)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq W$ open, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]). (1) If $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then $\mathcal F|_W$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module for every open $W\subseteq X$. (2) If $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module for every $i\in I$, then $\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. (Both conditions of [pqf-def-coherent] are local: being of finite type is a condition on neighbourhoods of points, and for the kernel condition over an open $W$ one restricts to the $W\cap U_i$, kernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules being computed sectionwise.)

source.place: Stacks, Sheaves of Modules, Definition 01BV (definition-coherent) and Definition 01B5 (definition-finite-type); the locality is used without statement in the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYJ (coherent-lemma-pushforward-coherent-on-open, literature/stacks-project/coherent.tex)

proof.text: Apply the finite-type locality core to obtain the two finite-type implications. These concern only the finite-type conjunct, not coherence of the restrictions or coherence of F.

For coherent F and an open W, the first core implication gives finite type of the restricted module. Project the kernel condition from coherence of F, and apply the kernel-condition restriction theorem. Pair these two conclusions using the definition of coherence.

For coherent restrictions on the cover, the second core implication gives finite type of F. Project their kernel conditions and apply single-kernel descent for every open W, rank n and map from the rank-n free module. Pair finite type and these kernel conditions using the definition of coherence.

proof_origin.place: Definitions 01BV and 01B5; original restriction/locality argument reduced to three strictly smaller statements. The finite-type core and both kernel-condition lemmas remain open: this is a decomposition, not an axiom-free proof.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ a covering by open subschemes; for an open $W\subseteq X$ write $\mathcal F|_W$ for the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to the open subscheme $W$ ($(\mathcal F|_W)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq W$ open). (1) If $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then $\mathcal F|_W$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module for every open $W\subseteq X$. (2) If $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module for every $i\in I$, then $\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. (Both conditions of [pqf-def-coherent] are local: being of finite type is a condition on neighbourhoods of points, and for the kernel condition over an open $W$ one restricts to the $W\cap U_i$, kernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules being computed sectionwise.)

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction to opens).* Throughout, a surjection of $\mathcal O_W$-modules means an epimorphism of the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$, and "of finite type" and "coherent" are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. For opens $V\subseteq W\subseteq X$ of the scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme]: (a) $\mathcal O_X|_W=\mathcal O_W$ and $(\mathcal G|_W)|_V=\mathcal G|_V$ for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, with $(\alpha|_W)|_V=\alpha|_V$ for morphisms: by the formula for restriction to an open subscheme (for inclusions of open subschemes $f(U)=U$ and $f^\sharp$ is the identity), both sides have sections $\mathcal G(V')$ over $V'\subseteq V$ open, the same restriction maps and the same $\mathcal O_X(V')$-action. (b) Restriction $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_V$, $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$, is a left adjoint, so it preserves coproducts, whence $(\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n})|_V\cong\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ by (a); and it preserves epimorphisms: if $e$ is an epimorphism and $g\circ e|_V=h\circ e|_V$, the adjoint transposes satisfy $g^\flat\circ e=h^\flat\circ e$, so $g^\flat=h^\flat$ and $g=h$. (c) For a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ of $\mathcal O_W$-modules, $\Ker(\varphi)|_V=\Ker(\varphi|_V)$: kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_W)$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$ are computed sectionwise, so both have sections $\ker(\varphi_{V'}:\mathcal G(V')\to\mathcal H(V'))$ over $V'\subseteq V$, with the same restriction maps and module structures. (d) Being of finite type is invariant under isomorphism (compose the surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ with the restricted isomorphism).

*Step 2 (finite type restricts).* Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type and $W\subseteq X$ open. For $x\in W$ choose by [pqf-def-coherent] an open $U\ni x$ of $X$ and a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$. Restricting it to the open $U\cap W$ gives by Step 1(a),(b) a surjection $\mathcal O_{U\cap W}^{\oplus n}\cong(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n})|_{U\cap W}\to\mathcal G|_{U\cap W}=(\mathcal G|_W)|_{U\cap W}$, and $U\cap W$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $W$. Hence $\mathcal G|_W$ is of finite type.

*Step 3 (part (1)).* Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent and $W\subseteq X$ open. $\mathcal F|_W$ is of finite type by Step 2. Let $W'\subseteq W$ be open and $\varphi:\mathcal O_{W'}^{\oplus n}\to(\mathcal F|_W)|_{W'}$ a morphism. By Step 1(a) $(\mathcal F|_W)|_{W'}=\mathcal F|_{W'}$, and $W'$ is open in $X$, so the kernel of $\varphi$ is of finite type by the kernel condition of [pqf-def-coherent] for $\mathcal F$. Hence $\mathcal F|_W$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module.

*Step 4 (finite type is local).* Let $W\subseteq X$ be open, $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ an open covering and $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_W$-module with $\mathcal G|_{W_i}$ of finite type for every $i$. For $x\in W$ pick $i$ with $x\in W_i$; by [pqf-def-coherent] for $\mathcal G|_{W_i}$ there are an open $V\ni x$ of $W_i$ and a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to(\mathcal G|_{W_i})|_V=\mathcal G|_V$ (Step 1(a)). $V$ is open in $W$, so $\mathcal G$ is of finite type.

*Step 5 (part (2)).* Let $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ be coherent for all $i$. $\mathcal F$ is of finite type by Step 4 (with $W=X$, $W_i=U_i$). Let $W\subseteq X$ be open and $\varphi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$ a morphism with kernel $\mathcal K$. Put $W_i=W\cap U_i$, an open of $U_i$; these cover $W$. By Step 1, $\mathcal K|_{W_i}=\Ker(\varphi|_{W_i})$ and $\varphi|_{W_i}$ is, up to the isomorphism $\mathcal O_{W_i}^{\oplus n}\cong(\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n})|_{W_i}$, a morphism $\mathcal O_{W_i}^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_{W_i}=(\mathcal F|_{U_i})|_{W_i}$; composing with an isomorphism of the source replaces the kernel by an isomorphic one. By the kernel condition of [pqf-def-coherent] for the coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ and its open $W_i$, this kernel is of finite type, hence so is $\mathcal K|_{W_i}$ (Step 1(d)). By Step 4, $\mathcal K$ is of finite type. So $\mathcal F$ satisfies both conditions of [pqf-def-coherent] and is coherent.
